verdict: Pass with source-boundary caveats. Public HearthRanger VisionAI pages support GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card CARDID.json behavior files, and optional Combo.json. HearthstoneJSON supports card metadata and option identities. The stronger HSConfig policy that normal prepare emits per-card files for every deck card is repo policy, not a directly documented HearthRanger requirement.
source_backed_claims: HearthRanger documents CustomConfig deck mapping through deck_config.ini and deck-specific directories.
GlobalValues.json is documented with GameCardId GlobalValues, condition/value rows, and FirstTurnValueWeight plus SecondTurnValueWeight board-value weighting.
Mulligan.json is documented with GameCardId Mulligan, Mulligan.values rows, mulligan selectors, condition, and hold/discard value.
Combo.json is documented with GameCardId Combo, ComboList.values, same-turn >>, and across-turn >-> syntax.
Per-card CARDID.json behavior files are documented with blocks such as InHandPlayPriority and OnDiscoverCardBonus; examples show condition/value rows.
HearthstoneJSON exposes latest card JSON data with card ids, dbfId, text, mechanics, referencedTags, entourage, playRequirements, and related metadata.
repo_evidence: src/hsconfig/surface_intent.py treats GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json as universal required surfaces.
src/hsconfig/package_builder.py emits per-card CardID files, always writes GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json, and writes Combo.json only when combo payload exists.
src/hsconfig/apply_gate.py defines load-safe apply around required GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json.
tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py proves normal prepare emits richer per-card files for the provided Wild decks.
no_block_implication: There is no public-doc reason to block a valid deck when only semantic richness is incomplete. HSConfig should continue to treat load_safe_apply as its own operator policy and not present it as a HearthRanger term.
mechanic_or_surface_gaps: Public proof exists for per-card behavior files, but not for an official requirement that every deck card must always have a per-card file.
Some accepted registry blocks need explicit source-gap annotation if they are not confirmed from public docs, including OnAdaptCardBonus, BeforeUpgradeCardBonus, and OnBoardPlayPriority.
Choose One option identity is plausible through HearthstoneJSON, but still requires exact mapping before lowering.
The public VisionAI pages are legacy-style and undated, so they are syntax evidence rather than a complete versioned contract.
bloat_or_scope_risk: Treating every-card CardID emission as official external requirement would overstate the evidence.
Expanding accepted VisionAI blocks without source tracking increases maintenance risk.
Calling load_safe_apply a HearthRanger concept rather than an HSConfig operator policy would blur responsibility.
recommended_next_actions: Keep the external surface contract phrased as documented core surfaces: GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card CARDID.json, and optional Combo.json.
Label per-card-every-card coverage as HSConfig rich-output repo policy.
Add source-gap notes for accepted registry blocks that are not confirmed from public docs.
Keep warning-only mechanics report-only unless exact documented VisionAI syntax and source-backed identity exist.
uncertain: Whether current live VisionAI supports every block accepted by HSConfig's registry.
Whether newer non-public HearthRanger documentation supersedes public help pages.
Whether per-card files for every deck card are practically necessary in runtime or simply useful rich output.
